question: What is the main sign of neurasthenia?

options.A: Chronic nervous exhaustion and physical fatigue
options.C: Sudden episodes of complete muscle paralysis
options.D: Severe cognitive decline and memory loss

explanation: You've got this! Neurasthenia is simply known as a condition of ongoing physical tiredness and nervous burnout. Keep up the great work!

question: Why do many patients in Nigeria often report body tiredness rather than emotional feelings?

options.A: Local climate conditions cause chronic physical fatigue
options.B: Cultural tendencies often express emotional distress through physical symptoms
options.C: Physical illness is the only recognized health issue in the region
options.D: Psychiatric disorders are strictly forbidden from having emotional symptoms

explanation: Spot on! This is called somatization—it's very common for people to show emotional stress through bodily aches and tiredness. You are learning fast!

question: Which sign shows mental fatigue in neurasthenia?
explanation: Great try! Mental tiredness directly affects your brain's ability to focus and remember things. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: A patient feels heavy, has aching muscles, and can't sleep well—yet tests show no physical disease. What matches this?
explanation: Brilliant! When physical weakness and poor sleep won't go away and tests are clear, it points straight to neurasthenia. You're doing awesome.

question: How do everyday stressors affect the development of neurasthenia?

options.A: They permanently alter brain chemistry instantly
options.B: They prevent any form of physical illness from occurring
options.C: They deplete coping reserves over time and trigger exhaustion
options.D: They have no impact on mental or physical health

explanation: You nailed it! Constant daily pressure slowly drains a person's nervous energy until they feel totally burnt out. Keep going!

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of neurasthenia?
explanation: Nice one! Eating healthy food doesn't cause nervous exhaustion. Money worries, work stress, and family pressures are the real triggers here.

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before confirming neurasthenia?

options.A: Medical conditions like anemia or infections share similar symptoms of fatigue
options.B: Laboratory tests can definitively measure the exact amount of nervous energy
options.C: Hospital policy requires a blood test for every single mental health visit
options.D: Physical illnesses are always cured by psychiatric medications

explanation: Spot on! We always rule out physical issues like low blood levels first, because conditions like anemia can make a patient feel just as tired. Great nursing logic!

question: What is an important goal when assessing a patient with neurasthenia?

options.A: Encouraging them to ignore all physical sensations
options.B: Proving to them that their symptoms are entirely imagined
options.C: Validating their experience of pain and building trust
options.D: Rushing through the interview to save hospital time

explanation: You're a natural! Patients often feel brushed off when lab tests come back normal. Believing their pain builds the trust they need to heal.

question: How does neurasthenia mainly differ from major depression?

options.A: Neurasthenia centers on physical fatigue rather than pervasive sadness and worthlessness
options.B: Depression never causes any physical tiredness or sleep changes
options.C: Depression is treated exclusively with physical exercise
options.D: Neurasthenia only occurs in children and teenagers

explanation: Fantastic! Neurasthenia is all about deep physical exhaustion, while depression is centered around deep sadness and hopelessness. You're crushing it!

question: What is the main focus of generalized anxiety disorder compared to neurasthenia?

options.A: Severe physical paralysis of the lower limbs
options.B: Excessive and uncontrollable worry about future events
options.C: Complete loss of memory regarding personal identity
options.D: Sudden bursts of intense physical energy

explanation: You got it! Anxiety is all about constant, runaway worry, whereas neurasthenia focuses on running out of nervous energy. Keep up the brilliant effort!

question: A patient with neurasthenia stays in bed all day from fatigue. What is the best first nursing step?

options.A: Advise complete bed rest for the next two weeks
options.B: Scold the patient for being lazy and unmotivated
options.C: Gradually encourage structured activity mixed with scheduled rest periods
options.D: Force the patient to run outside to build immediate stamina

explanation: Well done! Mixing gentle activity with planned rest stops their body from getting weaker while respecting their low energy. Perfect nursing care!

question: What is the main goal of stress management for someone with neurasthenia?

options.B: Teaching the patient how to ignore family members
options.C: Helping the patient identify triggers and use healthier coping skills

explanation: Spot on! Helping patients spot their stressors and handle them better stops total burnout before it happens. You are learning real clinical skills!

question: Why is teaching sleep hygiene so important in recovery?

options.A: It replaces the need for any nutritional counseling
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never feel tired again
options.C: It helps regulate rest patterns to restore depleted nervous energy

explanation: You're doing great! Good sleep habits give the tired nervous system the deep rest it needs to repair itself. Keep practicing daily!

question: What physical activity advice should a nurse give?

options.B: Engage in gentle, graduated exercise like walking
options.C: Only exercise when experiencing severe exhaustion
options.D: Avoid all forms of movement until fully recovered

explanation: Awesome job! Slow and steady exercise like walking boosts mood and stamina without draining their low energy reserves. You're ready for the wards!
